entries.name: title
entries.description: The agenda's name / a person's chosen name / a task, event, or note title.

entries.name: kind
entries.description: What this row IS -- the discriminator every card list filters on. `board` = the one agenda root row; `task` = something to do; `event` = something happening at a time; `member` = a person; `note` = a written note. DELIBERATELY has no default and is NOT required: rows created by machinery that cannot know the kind (the activity log's comment composer, and ICS import) leave it empty, and an empty kind keeps them out of every kind-filtered list while date-driven views (agenda/calendar/buckets/timeline) still show them.

entries.name: board
entries.description: Which board (a kind=board entry) this task/event/note belongs to -- stamped at creation from the `tasklyCurrentBoard` setting, alongside the `contains` edge to that same root. The edge is what the SHARE pipeline walks; this column is what the task VIEWS filter on. Both are stamped at write time because the engine has no derived fields, and neither can substitute for the other. DELIBERATELY empty on member rows and on activity-log comment rows: those are per-install/global, and a blank board value falls outside every board filter, which is exactly how the old kind-only filters kept them out of Today/Upcoming/Calendar/Long view/Map. Rows that predate this column are stamped `board_root` by the host's taskly migration, so nothing an existing user wrote disappears behind the new filters. HIDDEN from the record editor (like `type`/`order`/`isLogEntry`/`postedAt`/`createdBy`) because a visible ref picker over every board READS as a 'Move to board' control but is only half of one: changing it rewrites this column -- so the item leaves the old board's views -- while leaving the `contains` edge alone, so it stays in the old board's SHARE subtree. A task apparently moved out of a shared board would keep syncing to that board's members, silently. The real Move action now EXISTS (boardmgmt-0817) and rewrites both halves to the same destination in one host call -- `tasklyMoveItemToBoard` in isan's `lib/src/taskly_board_ops.dart`, fired from the Move-to-board screen; it stays host Dart rather than an applet-JSON chain because the engine has no conditional action, so "resolve the destination BEFORE touching either half" is not expressible in JSON, and a JSON chain would clear this column on an unresolved destination instead of no-op'ing. This field stays HIDDEN from the editor regardless: a bare ref picker would still be a half-move. Still SHOWN read-only on the Details screen, whose `record` names it in an explicit `fields` allow-list (which overrides `hidden`) -- so you can see which board an item is in, just not half-move it.

entries.name: status
entries.description: Task semantics: todo / doing / done. `done` is what every checkbox toggle writes and what the Completed bucket reads. Events use it too -- a past event you tick off reads as done.

entries.name: scheduledStart
entries.description: The day this happens (an event's start, or the day you have chosen to DO a task). The primary date across the agenda, calendar, and timeline. Named `scheduledStart` rather than `date` because two engine behaviors key off that exact name: toggleDone's recurrence only shifts columns literally named scheduledStart/endDate/due, and the host's ICS-import menu calls importIcs with no column overrides, so imported events land here.

entries.name: endDate
entries.description: Optional end day for something spanning several days. Also the timeline's bar end, and the second date ICS import writes for a multi-day event.

entries.name: due
entries.description: A task's deadline, as opposed to the day you plan to work on it (`scheduledStart`). The agenda and calendar fall back to this when a row has no start, so a due-only task still shows up on its day. Also shifted by recurrence.

entries.name: time
entries.description: Time of day as HH:MM (e.g. 09:30). Drives the agenda's within-day ordering and its leading time label. Rows with no time sort after timed ones, which is the right reading order for a day.

entries.name: endTime
entries.description: Optional end time of day as HH:MM. Display only -- the engine's calendar and ICS export are all-day-event based, so this is not exported to a calendar file.

entries.name: repeat
entries.description: Recurrence rule as `d:N` (every N days), `w:N` (every N weeks), or `m:N` (every N months) -- e.g. `w:1` for weekly. Blank means it happens once. Ticking a repeating row done materializes the NEXT occurrence with every date shifted by the rule; the completed row stays put as the history entry.

entries.name: category
entries.description: Free-text label for grouping and filtering (e.g. work, home, errands). Deliberately free text, not a fixed enum -- the filter options derive from whatever values your own rows actually use.

entries.name: place
entries.description: Where this happens, as a `lat, lng` string with a Pick-on-map button in the editor. `latColumn`/`lonColumn` ask the engine to mirror the picked point into the numeric lat/lon pair the Map screen plots. NOTE: the mirroring half of that rule is a concurrent engine change; on an engine that predates it the extra keys are inert data (the picker still fills this text field, and lat/lon can be typed by hand) -- nothing here breaks either way.

entries.name: lat
entries.description: Pin latitude. Only rows with BOTH lat and lon set appear on the Map screen; rows missing either are skipped silently, which is what you want for the many rows that have no location at all.

entries.name: lon
entries.description: Pin longitude. See `lat`.

entries.name: notes
entries.description: Freeform detail -- a note's body, or the extra context on a task or event. This is the column ICS export writes as the event description and ICS import reads one back into.

entries.name: author
entries.description: Which member (a kind=member entry) created this row -- stamped at creation from the per-install `tasklyMemberId` setting, NOT from sign-in identity, so attribution works with no account at all. Empty renders as 'Unattributed', which is a normal state (nobody has picked a card yet), not an error.

entries.name: initials
entries.description: A member's short badge, auto-derived from their typed name on save (Alex Kim -> AK; one letter for a one-word name; the given-name part for a Korean name). Still fully editable -- type your own and it sticks; clear it and it re-derives. Meaningless on non-member rows.

entries.name: color
entries.description: A member's chip color -- the thing that tells two people apart when their auto-derived badges collide.

entries.name: completed
entries.description: The day this was ticked done, stamped automatically by the checkbox toggle and cleared automatically if you un-tick it. Not hand-edited in normal use.

entries.name: completedTime
entries.description: The HH:MM companion to `completed`, stamped and cleared by the same toggle. Hidden from the editor -- it is bookkeeping, not something to type.

entries.name: editedBy
entries.description: Who last MEANINGFULLY revised this -- stamped on a save that actually changes a field, and by an inline edit in the activity log. Distinct from `author`, which never changes after creation.

entries.name: editedAt
entries.description: The day of that last meaningful revision. Also stamped on a row when someone posts to its activity log, so an item with fresh discussion but no field change still surfaces as recently touched. Distinct from the engine's own `updatedAt`, which is rewritten on every save including trivial ones.

entries.name: comment
entries.description: The body of an activity-log entry -- the 'why' behind a change, written in the log rather than buried in the item's notes.

entries.name: postedAt
entries.description: The precise instant a log comment was posted, stamped once and never touched again -- what the log's relative '2h ago' line reads. Hidden from the editor.

entries.name: isLogEntry
entries.description: Stamped true automatically on every row the activity log's composer creates, marking it as discussion rather than a first-class agenda item. Hidden from the editor.

entries.name: type
entries.description: Compatibility discriminator for the SHARE pipeline only (isan's share_sink.dart levelMayPush checks Dispatch's `type` vocabulary, not this app's own `kind`), and the value the activity log stamps on the entries it creates. Mirrors tripboard/krtravelplan. Never shown in the record editor.

entries.name: order
entries.description: Sort position within an activity log thread. Managed by the log; hidden from the editor.

entries.name: source
entries.description: Where this row came from: `local` for anything you added in the app, `ics` for a row created by the host's "Import calendar (.ics)" menu item (stamped via the applet manifest's `icsImport.values`). Blank means 'created before this column existed', not 'local'.

entries.name: updatedAt
entries.description: The engine's own auto-stamped per-row write time (ISO-8601, stamped by the reserved key name regardless of declared type). DISPLAY-ONLY -- last-write-wins reserved, silently overwritten on every save, never listed as an editable value.

entries.name: createdBy
entries.description: Signed-in PocketBase user id when signed in, else this install's stable local actor id ($playerId) -- stamped at creation on every add action, used ONLY by the sharing pipeline's per-row 'own row' gate so a commenter-level collaborator can push the rows they themselves wrote. Separate from `author`, this app's own member attribution, which must never key off sign-in. Never shown in the record editor.

relations.name: fromId
relations.description: The source node of this relationship (the agenda root, for every edge in v2).

relations.name: toId
relations.description: The target node of this relationship (the member/task/event/note it links in).

relations.name: type
relations.description: `contains` is the only edge type needed: structural agenda-root -> item, walked by the share pipeline's subtree closure. An item with no contains edge back to the root is invisible to sharing.
